source_matrix.title: Apache Calcite Materialized Views
source_matrix.reading_this_turn: View rewriting introduction, structural rewriting and constraint support
source_matrix.covered: Equivalence-based view substitution, residual filtering, aggregation rollup and partial rewriting; declared keys and constraints support rewrites.
source_matrix.our_inference: Rejecting a lossy name-only projection for entity counting is not itself a novel agent algorithm. A formal optimizer consumes a query; it does not independently establish that an upstream generated query matches a natural-language request.
source_matrix.not_claimed: No new Calcite execution on this exact clarified pair this turn; documentation is not proof that every expression shape is supported.

source_matrix.title: CostBench: Evaluating Multi-Turn Cost-Optimal Planning and Adaptation in Dynamic Environments for LLM Tool-Use Agents
source_matrix.publication_status: ACL 2026 long paper, official proceedings metadata
source_matrix.covered: Cost-aware planning using atomic/composite tools and adaptation to cost changes or failures in travel planning.
source_matrix.our_inference: A cheaper but correct alternative plan, or a different first tool choice, is not sufficient evidence of demand reinterpretation. A pure planning result overlaps this existing evaluation axis.
source_matrix.not_claimed: No reproduction, full-paper re-review or imported numerical performance claims.

source_matrix.title: How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior
source_matrix.publication_status: ACL 2026 long paper, official proceedings metadata
source_matrix.covered: Experience-following, error propagation and misaligned experience replay, including misleading value from apparently correct past executions.
source_matrix.our_inference: A correct history being harmful to a later task is already a close topic. Potential additional evidence would require controlled availability/price effects on observable demand interpretation, not merely a new cache-error example.
source_matrix.not_claimed: No claim of first discovery, absence of closer work, independent replication or verified equivalence of task settings.

fair_baseline_input_gate.inputs: Same current reviewed task, schema and accessible fixed database; generate the query from those inputs, not from the hidden reference SQL.
fair_baseline_input_gate.costs: All generation, failed tools and recomputation; equal successful-solution feasibility.
fair_baseline_input_gate.interpretation: Measures whether ordinary direct solving suffices. Existing unavailable-cache cells retain history context and are not automatically an independent no-history baseline.

fair_baseline_input_gate.inputs: The approved four-cell protocol; same common task/history text, tool capabilities and correctness instruction.
fair_baseline_input_gate.interpretation: Current batch observes actions and answers, not a temporally prior explicit task contract.

fair_baseline_input_gate.inputs: Model constructs its own contract from the current request before reuse planning; it does not receive a hidden gold contract or reference program unavailable to competitors.
fair_baseline_input_gate.costs: Extra contract generation and verification included.
fair_baseline_input_gate.interpretation: A future separately frozen method comparison, not a post-hoc modification of the ordinary workflow. Contract elicitation and ordering can change behavior.

fair_baseline_input_gate.inputs: Original current request and necessary public schema/history facts, candidate interpretation/query; no scorer label or expected numeric answer.
fair_baseline_input_gate.costs: Verification plus any repair or recomputation included.
fair_baseline_input_gate.interpretation: Tests a strong existing safeguard; verification success must not be portrayed as a new named algorithm.

fair_baseline_input_gate.inputs: Same upstream-generated current query/contract and trusted history definition; only genuinely declared constraints, never assumed name uniqueness.
fair_baseline_input_gate.interpretation: Can reject incompatible view reuse, but query-equivalence preservation alone cannot correct a query that already encodes the wrong user request.

fair_baseline_input_gate.inputs: Human-confirmed/reference current query explicitly supplied as oracle information.
fair_baseline_input_gate.interpretation: Useful to localize downstream tool correctness or feasibility; not a fair primary end-to-end method when competitors must infer the current query. Report separately.

outcome_contingent_next_step_memo.observation: All four conditions correct, with the same or different legitimate routes
outcome_contingent_next_step_memo.interpretation: This development case does not demonstrate the proposed failure. Route/cost adaptation alone is not drift.
outcome_contingent_next_step_memo.next: Do not enlarge this case by repeatedly changing prices, prompts or seeds until it fails. Review evidence for further independently justified task screening; no automatic new paid batch.

outcome_contingent_next_step_memo.observation: Wrong scalar or inappropriate name-cache row counting
outcome_contingent_next_step_memo.interpretation: Observed task error, not automatically C-type demand drift. The formal information-loss boundary remains covered by strong applicability checking.
outcome_contingent_next_step_memo.next: Review original task, generated program and tool exposure to separate A/B/D/E or undetermined cause. A future C-type diagnostic needs observable prior task interpretation and independently reviewed subsequent behavior.

outcome_contingent_next_step_memo.observation: A price/availability contrast in this single pair
outcome_contingent_next_step_memo.interpretation: A descriptive development contrast only; one task and one realization do not establish a general effect or isolate interpretation from downstream information exposure.
outcome_contingent_next_step_memo.next: Do not present significance or causal internal-state claims. Any later confirmation must freeze independent tasks and sampling before results.

outcome_contingent_next_step_memo.observation: Prose answers, abstentions, malformed output or infrastructure stop
outcome_contingent_next_step_memo.interpretation: Use the frozen separate dispositions and whole-batch audit. Unclear prose is not automatically wrong; infrastructure failure is not semantic evidence.
outcome_contingent_next_step_memo.next: Preserve all records and pending reviews; no silent replacement or successful-prefix effect estimate.

method_innovation_gate: Before proposing a method, demonstrate a remaining quality-versus-total-cost gap after fair contract-first, independent-verifier and applicability/recompute baselines. Oracle SQL, all-cache rejection or a one-off name-count rule cannot establish the desired end-to-end increment.
